sentences.text: The Kisan Maandhan Yojana (KMYM) is a pension scheme launched by the Government of India.
It aims to provide social security to small and marginal farmers.
The scheme was introduced to ensure a steady income for farmers post-retirement.
The initiative is part of the government's broader efforts to enhance the welfare of the agricultural community.
The primary objective of KMYM is to provide a pension of Rs. 3,000 per month to eligible farmers.
This pension is intended to support farmers who have contributed to the agricultural sector throughout their lives.
The scheme also aims to reduce the financial burden on farmers during their old age.
Benefits under KMYM include a monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 after the age of 60.
Farmers who enroll in the scheme will receive financial assistance that can help meet their basic needs.
The scheme also provides for the spouse of the farmer in case of the farmer's death.
In such cases, the spouse will receive 50% of the pension amount.
Eligibility criteria for KMYM include being a small or marginal farmer.
The applicant must be between the ages of 18 and 40 years at the time of enrollment.
The farmer must have landholding of up to 2 hectares.
The scheme is targeted towards those who are not covered under any other pension scheme.
Farmers must also have a valid Aadhaar number for identification purposes.
The application process for KMYM is straightforward.
Farmers can apply online through the official PM-KMY portal.
They can also visit the nearest Common Service Center (CSC) for assistance.
The application requires basic details such as name, age, and landholding information.
Farmers must also provide their Aadhaar details during the application process.
Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the concerned authorities.
The pension will be disbursed on a monthly basis once the farmer reaches the age of 60.
The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.
State governments also play a role in the implementation of the scheme.
The government has set a target to enroll a significant number of farmers under this scheme.
The enrollment process is ongoing and farmers can apply at any time.
The scheme is expected to benefit millions of farmers across the country.
